answer.value: Truncation: 4.4% of Track A generations hit the 2048-token cap, so the macro gate is indicative rather than exact. Scope is limited to formal logic; code generation and tool use not evaluated. Not a chat model: no safety tuning beyond the base model's and no instruction-following alignment (IFEval regressed slightly). A short generation budget truncates the <think> reasoning and scores far worse.
quotes:
At a 2048-token budget, 4.4% of Track A generations hit the cap — better than
the base's 17.4%, but still above the 2% threshold our protocol requires to mark a comparison
`rankable`.
The Track A macro gate should therefore be read as indicative rather than exact.

The Track B suite does not cover code generation or tool use
(HumanEval, LiveCodeBench and BFCL were not run for this model or its base), so this release
makes no claim about those.

It has had no
safety tuning beyond whatever the base model carries, and no instruction-following alignment
work — IFEval regressed slightly.

The model opens a `<think>...</think>` reasoning block
before answering, so a short generation budget truncates reasoning and scores far worse.
